idiom_name: SimpleDelegator subclass + identity Hash (compare_by_identity) + revoke flag
implementation_notes: Ruby ships delegation in the standard library: Delegator forwards every method it does not define through method_missing and deliberately delegates the identity operators (!, ==, !=) to __getobj__, and SimpleDelegator subclasses it so the wrapped object can be swapped at run time (ruby-doc.org). A membrane is then a Delegator subclass plus a wrap method for arguments, results and blocks, an identity map (a Hash with compare_by_identity, or a WeakMap) and a revoke flag checked before every forward. What the standard library does not give you is the policy: it forwards transparently, including whatever reaches the raw target through reflective calls, and method_missing is the only hook - so completeness stays the membrane's responsibility, and the classic per-method forwarding is justified whenever calls must be mediated method by method.
pitfalls: method_missing is the only hook: methods Delegator itself defines (including == and !) are not forwarded, and respond_to_missing? must be implemented as well or introspection disagrees with behaviour.

The identity map must use compare_by_identity (or WeakMap keyed on the raw object): a normal Hash calls hash/eql?, which merges value-equal targets and can recurse back through the delegator for delegator arguments.

Transparency cuts both ways: instance_variable_get, send(:__getobj__) and similar reflective calls reach the raw target from inside the mediated surface, so delegation mediates ordinary calls, not reflective ones.

variants.name: BasicObject + method_missing (hand-controlled surface)
variants.idiom_name: membrane class inheriting BasicObject with method_missing and explicit core methods
variants.implementation_notes: Implementing the membrane directly on BasicObject - the near-empty parent of every Ruby class - removes the inherited method set from the wrapper, so nothing leaks through methods the wrapper itself defines, and every operation the guest can perform is a method the membrane chose to answer via method_missing or to define explicitly (ruby-doc.org). This costs the conveniences (no is_a?, no respond_to?, no inspect unless you write them) and buys a surface you control completely, which is what a security boundary wants; it also makes deliberate choices necessary about identity (==, equal?, hash) that SimpleDelegator would otherwise decide for you. Choose this variant when the mediated surface must be an allow-list, the stdlib variant when transparent delegation is the goal.
pitfalls: BasicObject lacks Kernel, Object#inspect and even is_a?: diagnostics and library code that assume Object (pp, RSpec matchers, JSON encoders) will fail or misbehave on the wrapper unless the needed methods are defined deliberately.

Reflective escapes are only closed if you close them: __send__, instance_variable_get and ObjectSpace are still reachable through ::Kernel/Object constants unless the membrane decides about them, and BasicObject does not hide the ivars.
Identity semantics must be chosen explicitly (==, equal?, hash, eql?): define them on the wrapper or the membrane silently changes how the wrapped object behaves in sets and hashes.
